children.text: Study charged particles in the terrestrial magnetosphere. Use \(c=2.998\times10^8\,\mathrm{m/s}\), \(\epsilon_0=8.9\times10^{-12}\), \(\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}\), \(e=1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm C\), electron mass \(m=9.1\times10^{-31}\,\mathrm{kg}\), proton mass \(m_p=1.67\times10^{-27}\,\mathrm{kg}\), \(k=1.38\times10^{-23}\), \(g=9.8\,\mathrm{m/s^2}\), \(h=6.626\times10^{-34}\), \(R_E=6.4\times10^6\,\mathrm m\), and equatorial surface dipole strength \(B_0=3.1\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm T\). For a dipole directed down the z axis, use \[\mathbf B_d=\frac{B_0R_E^3}{r^5}[-3xz\hat{\mathbf x}-3yz\hat{\mathbf y}+(x^2+y^2-2z^2)\hat{\mathbf z}],\quad r\ge R_E.\] The original statement prints a plus sign on the x term, inconsistent with an axial dipole and the later solution. The corrected dipole convention is explicit here. Dayside reconnection permits some solar-wind particles to reach the magnetotail and subsequently precipitate into the thermosphere.

children.text: An electron starts at the origin with velocity \(v\hat{\mathbf y}\) perpendicular to uniform \(\mathbf B=B\hat{\mathbf z}\). Find its trajectory.
Find the current magnitude and the electron orbital magnetic-moment vector.
If the initial velocity makes angle \(0<\theta<90^\circ\) with B, find the helix pitch.
In uniform B along z, ions and electrons have equal temperature and density \(n(x)=n_0+\alpha x\), with \(\alpha>0\). Explain the current generation with a sketch. Pressure is \(p=2knT\).
For Maxwellian ions and electrons, find beta in the signed magnetization \(M=\beta n(x)kT/B\). You may use \(\int_0^\infty xe^{-x}dx=1\) and \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}e^{-x^2}dx=\sqrt\pi\).

At \((x,y,z)=(10R_E,0,R_E)\), use \(p(z)=p_0e^{-(z/a)^2}\), \(p_0=3\times10^{-10}\,\mathrm{Pa}\), \(a=2R_E\), and local \(B_{dia}=\mu_0M\). Calculate the ratio of diamagnetic and dipole field magnitudes, noting the different field-axis orientation from part b.

nodes.alt: Original field minimum P2 and maxima P1 P3 with converging field lines.

children.text: For a slowly varying magnetic mirror, \(\langle B_r\rangle=-r_c(dB/ds)/2\), with \(|B_r|\ll B_z\). Derive the gyro-averaged parallel force and show that \(\mu=mv_\perp^2/(2B)\) is conserved.
At the field minimum Bmin the pitch angle is theta. The mirror maximum is Bmax. Find the trapping condition.

nodes.alt: Original dipole field line and particle starting at the equatorial radius.

children.text: A particle starts at the equator at x=6RE with pitch theta. In the dipole approximation and ignoring drift, determine the pitch-angle condition for it to reach below 200 km near latitude 60 degrees.
Assume isothermal ideal gas with \(\rho_0g/P_0=0.13\,\mathrm{km^{-1}}\). Find density versus altitude and the oxygen-density ratio at 160 and 220 km.

nodes.alt: Original oxygen ground and two excited states with their energies and lifetimes.

children.text: Oxygen excited states lie 1.96 and 4.17 eV above ground, with lifetimes 110 s and 0.8 s. Collision frequency is \(\nu=10^9\rho/\rho_0\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\). Predict colours at 160 and 220 km.

Find the minimum solar-wind speed pushing the dayside magnetopause to geosynchronous radius. The wind has field \(B_s=5\times10^{-9}\,\mathrm T\) and density 50 protons per cubic centimetre. Ignore inner plasma pressure and changes of the dipole. Use the stated energy-density balance with magnetic pressure \(B^2/(2\mu_0)\).

statement.text:
Solar Wind and Aurora
Study charged particles in the terrestrial magnetosphere. Use \(c=2.998\times10^8\,\mathrm{m/s}\), \(\epsilon_0=8.9\times10^{-12}\), \(\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}\), \(e=1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm C\), electron mass \(m=9.1\times10^{-31}\,\mathrm{kg}\), proton mass \(m_p=1.67\times10^{-27}\,\mathrm{kg}\), \(k=1.38\times10^{-23}\), \(g=9.8\,\mathrm{m/s^2}\), \(h=6.626\times10^{-34}\), \(R_E=6.4\times10^6\,\mathrm m\), and equatorial surface dipole strength \(B_0=3.1\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm T\). For a dipole directed down the z axis, use \[\mathbf B_d=\frac{B_0R_E^3}{r^5}[-3xz\hat{\mathbf x}-3yz\hat{\mathbf y}+(x^2+y^2-2z^2)\hat{\mathbf z}],\quad r\ge R_E.\] The original statement prints a plus sign on the x term, inconsistent with an axial dipole and the later solution. The corrected dipole convention is explicit here. Dayside reconnection permits some solar-wind particles to reach the magnetotail and subsequently precipitate into the thermosphere.
a.i. Electron gyro-orbit

An electron starts at the origin with velocity \(v\hat{\mathbf y}\) perpendicular to uniform \(\mathbf B=B\hat{\mathbf z}\). Find its trajectory.
a.ii. Current and magnetic moment
Find the current magnitude and the electron orbital magnetic-moment vector.
a.iii. Helical pitch
If the initial velocity makes angle \(0<\theta<90^\circ\) with B, find the helix pitch.
b.i. Diamagnetic current
In uniform B along z, ions and electrons have equal temperature and density \(n(x)=n_0+\alpha x\), with \(\alpha>0\). Explain the current generation with a sketch. Pressure is \(p=2knT\).
b.ii. Plasma magnetization
For Maxwellian ions and electrons, find beta in the signed magnetization \(M=\beta n(x)kT/B\). You may use \(\int_0^\infty xe^{-x}dx=1\) and \(\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}e^{-x^2}dx=\sqrt\pi\).
c. Diamagnetic field ratio
At \((x,y,z)=(10R_E,0,R_E)\), use \(p(z)=p_0e^{-(z/a)^2}\), \(p_0=3\times10^{-10}\,\mathrm{Pa}\), \(a=2R_E\), and local \(B_{dia}=\mu_0M\). Calculate the ratio of diamagnetic and dipole field magnitudes, noting the different field-axis orientation from part b.
d.i. Adiabatic magnetic moment

For a slowly varying magnetic mirror, \(\langle B_r\rangle=-r_c(dB/ds)/2\), with \(|B_r|\ll B_z\). Derive the gyro-averaged parallel force and show that \(\mu=mv_\perp^2/(2B)\) is conserved.
d.ii. Mirror confinement
At the field minimum Bmin the pitch angle is theta. The mirror maximum is Bmax. Find the trapping condition.
e. Auroral loss cone

A particle starts at the equator at x=6RE with pitch theta. In the dipole approximation and ignoring drift, determine the pitch-angle condition for it to reach below 200 km near latitude 60 degrees.
f.i. Atmospheric stratification
Assume isothermal ideal gas with \(\rho_0g/P_0=0.13\,\mathrm{km^{-1}}\). Find density versus altitude and the oxygen-density ratio at 160 and 220 km.
f.ii. Auroral colours

Oxygen excited states lie 1.96 and 4.17 eV above ground, with lifetimes 110 s and 0.8 s. Collision frequency is \(\nu=10^9\rho/\rho_0\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\). Predict colours at 160 and 220 km.
g. Solar-wind compression
Find the minimum solar-wind speed pushing the dayside magnetopause to geosynchronous radius. The wind has field \(B_s=5\times10^{-9}\,\mathrm T\) and density 50 protons per cubic centimetre. Ignore inner plasma pressure and changes of the dipole. Use the stated energy-density balance with magnetic pressure \(B^2/(2\mu_0)\).

children.text: Let \(\omega_c=eB/m>0\), \(r_c=mv/(eB)\). Newton gives \(\dot v_x=-\omega_cv_y,\dot v_y=\omega_cv_x\). With the prescribed initial conditions, \[x=r_c(\cos\omega_ct-1),\quad y=r_c\sin\omega_ct,\quad z=0.\] It is a circle centred at \((-r_c,0)\), not at the initial position. The source unshifted circle misses the origin condition.
\(I=e/T=e^2B/(2\pi m)\). The conventional current circulates opposite to the electron, so \[\boldsymbol\mu=-\frac{mv_\perp^2}{2B}\hat{\mathbf B}.\] It is diamagnetic.
The parallel speed stays \(v\cos\theta\); multiply it by \(2\pi m/(eB)\). The pitch is \(2\pi mv\cos\theta/(eB)\), with orbit radius \(mv\sin\theta/(eB)\).

Opposite gyration senses and more guiding centres on the denser side produce charge currents in the same transverse direction. Magnetization is \(\mathbf M=-(p/B)\hat{\mathbf z}\), so \(\mathbf j_M=\nabla\times\mathbf M=(2kT\alpha/B)\hat{\mathbf y}\). Draw excess conventional current along positive y. This satisfies \(\mathbf j\times\mathbf B=\nabla p\).
For either species, \(\langle mv_\perp^2/2\rangle=kT\). Each therefore contributes \(-nkT/B\) along B. Together \(M=-2nkT/B=-p/B\), giving beta=-2.

Use \(|\mathbf B_d|^2=B_0^2(30^2+98^2)/101^5\). Then \(|B_{dia}|/|B_d|=\mu_0p/|B_d|^2\simeq0.306\). The source value about one divides by the squared x component alone. That is not the total dipole-field magnitude. The local magnetization opposes the total local field, so use its full magnitude unless a projected-component ratio is explicitly requested.

Gyro-averaging the axial Lorentz force gives \(F_\parallel=-\mu\,dB/ds\), where mu is the positive moment magnitude. Then \(d(mv_\parallel^2/2)/dt=-\mu\,dB/dt\). Total kinetic energy is constant, while perpendicular energy is \(\mu B\). Its derivative must be \(\mu\,dB/dt\), so \(B\,d\mu/dt=0\). Thus mu is adiabatically conserved under the stated slow-field approximation.

At reflection \(v_\parallel=0\). Energy and mu conservation give \(\sin^2\theta\ge B_{min}/B_{max}\). Thus \[\theta\ge\arcsin\sqrt{B_{min}/B_{max}}.\] The source final arcsine omits the square root, although its preceding velocity inequality requires it.

The initial strength is \(B_i=B_0/216\). At \(r=R_E+200\,\mathrm{km}\), latitude 60 degrees, \(B_L=B_0(R_E/r)^3\sqrt{1+3\sin^260^\circ}\). To avoid mirroring above that level, \(\sin^2\theta<B_i/B_L\), yielding roughly \(\theta<3.0^\circ\). Neglecting the 200 km altitude gives about 2.9 degrees. A single ideal dipole line from 6RE reaches the surface nearer 66 degrees, so the source specified latitude is an approximate target-field estimate rather than an exact field-line intersection.

With constant g over the height range, hydrostatic balance gives \(\rho(H)=\rho_0e^{-0.13H}\), H in km. Hence \(\rho(160)/\rho(220)=e^{7.8}=2.44\times10^3\). Keeping inverse-square gravity instead gives \(\rho/\rho_0=\exp[-(\rho_0gR_E/P_0)(1-R_E/(R_E+H))]\).

At 160 km, \(\nu\simeq0.93\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\), quenching the long-lived first state while the short-lived second state can radiate to the first. The photon has energy 2.21 eV and wavelength about 562 nm, green. At 220 km, \(\nu\simeq3.8\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\), so the first state survives and can radiate to ground at about 633 nm, red. The source assumes the lower excited state is more populated to identify the dominant red light. Other lines can still occur.

For a 24-hour period, \(r_g^3=gR_E^2(86400/(2\pi))^2\), so \(r_g\simeq6.59R_E\). Local dipole field is \(B_m=B_0(R_E/r_g)^3\). The model balance is \(\rho_sv^2/2+B_s^2/(2\mu_0)=B_m^2/(2\mu_0)\), with \(\rho_s=50\times10^6m_p\). Hence \[v=\sqrt{(B_m^2-B_s^2)/(\mu_0\rho_s)}\simeq330\,\mathrm{km/s}.\] This uses the source energy-density convention. A fluid momentum-flux pressure convention would replace the one-half kinetic factor and give a different threshold.
